title: 'HADOOP-18071. ABFS: Set driver global timeout for ITestAzureBlobFileSystemBasics'
category: test
requirement: '## Context

  This is test-harness hardening for Azure Blob Filesystem basics coverage, intended to cap flakiness without changing any user-visible ABFS behavior.

  ## Desired outcome

  The suite should enforce a stable overall timeout while continuing to exercise the same filesystem contract.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The test coverage remains the same, and the suite now runs under the intended global timeout policy instead of relying on more fragile timing defaults.

  '

Your PR title ...')?\n- [x] Object storage: have the integration tests been executed and the endpoint declared according to the connector-specific documentation?\n- [ ] If adding new dependencies to the code, are these dependencies licensed in a way that is compatible for inclusion under [ASF 2.0](http://www.apache.org/legal/resolved.html#category-a)?\n- [ ] If applicable, have you updated the `LICENSE`, `LICENSE-binary`, `NOTICE-binary` files?\n"

FILE: abfs-rename-metadata-recovery.yaml
title: HADOOP-18242. ABFS Rename Failure when tracking metadata is in an incomplete state
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  ABFS users need rename to recover safely when metadata is left in an incomplete intermediate state rather than returning a confusing partial result.

  ## Desired outcome

  Rename should distinguish recovery from hard failure, preserve the final source/destination outcome, and expose operational counters for `rename_recovery`, `metadata_incomplete_rename_failures`, and `rename_path_attempts`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Successful recovery leaves the destination present and source absent, failed recovery is surfaced clearly, and the new rename statistics reflect what actually happened.

  '

FILE: abfs-rename-recovery-removal.yaml
title: HADOOP-18002. abfs rename idempotency broken -remove recovery
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  ABFS clients currently try to recover ambiguous rename results by comparing modification times, but operators cannot rely on that signal because rename does not update object modification time. Keeping that recovery path in the client makes rename behavior look safer than it really is and adds unnecessary I/O.


  ## Desired outcome

  Remove the built-in modtime-based rename recovery path from the ABFS client and keep rename as a direct operation without that false idempotency check. Workloads that need rename recovery should use the etag-based approach outside the client instead of expecting the filesystem to guess the outcome.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Normal rename scenarios continue to behave the same, but the client no longer performs the deleted modtime recovery logic or advertises that path as the way to recover uncertain rename outcomes.

  '

FILE: abstractcsqueue-field-grouping.yaml
title: 'YARN-10904. Investigate: Remove unnecessary fields from AbstractCSQueue or group fields by feature if possible'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  CapacityScheduler queue objects currently mix path, allocation, and preemption state in ways that make scheduler maintenance fragile.


  ## Desired outcome

  Reorganize that internal state into clearer queue-path, allocation, and preemption groupings while preserving queue validation, inherited limits, and the scheduler behavior administrators already depend on.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Queue path creation, max-allocation validation, node-label checks, and preemption settings continue to behave exactly as before after the cleanup.

  '

item.text: I’ve confirmed the history contains the target JIRA subjects. Now I’m generating a full requirement-to-commit coverage report before I start applying anything, because the right automation depends on how many slugs map cleanly and where the outliers are.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
import os, re, subprocess, json
from pathlib import Path
req_dir = Path('/workspace/requirements')
branches = ['upstream/branch-3.3','upstream/branch-3.4','upstream/trunk']
logs = {}
for br in branches:
    out = subprocess.check_output(['git','-C','/workspace','log','--format=%H\\t%ad\\t%s','--date=short',br], text=True)
    entries = []
    for line in out.splitlines():
        h,d,s = line.split('\\t',2)
        entries.append((h,d,s))
    logs[br]=entries

reqs=[]
for f in sorted(req_dir.glob('*.yaml')):
    text=f.read_text()
    m=re.search(r'"'^title:'"\\s*(.*)"'$'"', text, re.M)
    title=m.group(1).strip() if m else ''
    jira_ids=re.findall(r'([A-Z]+-\\d+)', title)
    if not jira_ids:
        jira_ids=re.findall(r'([A-Z]+-\\d+)', text[:500])
    reqs.append((f.stem,title,jira_ids[0] if jira_ids else None))

summary=[]
zero=[]
mult=[]
for slug,title,jira in reqs:
    branch_hits={}
    total=0
    for br,entries in logs.items():
        hits=[]
        if jira:
            hits=[(h,d,s) for h,d,s in entries if jira in s]
        branch_hits[br]=hits[:5]
        total += len(hits)
    matched_branches={br:len(hits) for br,hits in branch_hits.items() if hits}
    item={'slug':slug,'jira':jira,'title':title,'matched_branches':matched_branches,'samples':{br:hits[:2] for br,hits in branch_hits.items() if hits}}
    summary.append(item)
    if total==0:
        zero.append(item)
    elif total>3:
        mult.append(item)
print('requirements', len(reqs))
print('zero_matches', len(zero))
for item in zero[:50]:
    print('ZERO', item['slug'], item['jira'], item['title'])
print('multi_gt3', len(mult))
for item in mult[:50]:
    print('MULTI', item['slug'], item['jira'], item['matched_branches'])
# branch availability counts
for br in branches:
    count=sum(1 for item in summary if br in item['matched_branches'])
    print('branch_coverage', br, count)
# write full json in /tmp for later inspection
Path('/tmp/requirement_commit_summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
print('wrote /tmp/requirement_commit_summary.json')
PY"

import os, re, subprocess, json
from pathlib import Path

    entries = []
    for line in out.splitlines():
        h,d,s = line.split('\\t',2)
        entries.append((h,d,s))
    logs[br]=entries

reqs=[]
for f in sorted(req_dir.glob('*.yaml')):
    text=f.read_text()
    m=re.search(r'"'^title:'"\\s*(.*)"'$'"', text, re.M)
    title=m.group(1).strip() if m else ''
    jira_ids=re.findall(r'([A-Z]+-\\d+)', title)
    if not jira_ids:
        jira_ids=re.findall(r'([A-Z]+-\\d+)', text[:500])
    reqs.append((f.stem,title,jira_ids[0] if jira_ids else None))

summary=[]
zero=[]

    total=0
    for br,entries in logs.items():

        branch_hits[br]=hits[:5]

    item={'slug':slug,'jira':jira,'title':title,'matched_branches':matched_branches,'samples':{br:hits[:2] for br,hits in branch_hits.items() if hits}}

title: HDFS-16422. Fix thread safety of EC decoding during concurrent preads
category: bugfix
requirement: 'HDFS-16422. Fix thread safety of EC decoding during concurrent preads


  Reading data on an erasure-coded file with missing replicas(internal block of block group) will cause online reconstruction: read `dataUnits` part of data and decode them into the target missing data. Each `DFSStripedInputStream` object has a `RawErasureDecoder` object, and when we doing pread concurrently, `RawErasureDecoder.decode` will be invoked concurrently too. `RawErasureDecoder.decode` is not thread safe, as a result of that we get wrong data from pread occasionally.

  '

title: HADOOP-18060.RPCMetrics increases the number of handlers in processing.
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators can already see how many RPC handler threads exist, but they cannot tell how many are actively working on requests at a given moment.

  ## Desired outcome

  RPC metrics should expose the current in-flight handler count through a dedicated metric instead of leaving this as an operational blind spot.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The metric name is `NumInProcessHandler`, it reports `0` when the server is idle, rises while handlers are actively processing calls, and falls back when those calls complete.

  '

FILE:kubernetes-datanode-locality
title: HDFS-16540 Data locality is lost when DataNode pod restarts in kubern…
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  In Kubernetes-style deployments, a DataNode pod can restart with the same DataNode identity but a different IP address. If the NameNode keeps the old host-to-DataNode mapping around, clients and colocated services can lose data locality because the stale IP is still treated as the preferred host.


  ## Desired outcome

  When a DataNode re-registers with the same UUID but a new IP address, the NameNode should replace the old host mapping with the new one so locality decisions follow the live pod location. This should preserve the existing registration semantics while ensuring stale IP entries do not continue to influence host lookups or block-location ordering.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Re-registration with the same DataNode identity removes the obsolete host entry, the new IP becomes the active host mapping for that DataNode, locality-sensitive block locations prefer the current IP rather than the stale one, and restarting a DataNode pod no longer causes persistent locality loss.

  '

title: Revert "HADOOP-17995. Stale record should be remove when DataNodePeerMetrics#dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson"
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  The recent change to aggressively prune stale entries from DataNode peer downstream timing JSON removed visibility that some operators and tests still depend on. This cleanup needs to be backed out until a safer semantics is defined.


  ## Desired outcome

  Revert the stale-record filtering change for DataNodePeerMetrics JSON output and restore the previous rolling-average behavior. This is an internal rollback intended to preserve existing observability contracts rather than introduce a new user-facing feature.

  The peer timing JSON behaves the way it did before the reverted change, and the attempted stale-entry pruning no longer alters that exported view.

FILE:remove-stale-peer-metrics
title: HADOOP-17995. Stale record should be remove when DataNodePeerMetrics#dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using DataNodePeerMetrics need dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson() to reflect only currently valid peer timing data. Stale entries should disappear once their rolling-average windows expire, otherwise the JSON keeps advertising dead peers as active.


  ## Desired outcome

  Restore stale-record removal for the peer downstream timing JSON while keeping active peers visible until their data truly expires. This should apply to the JSON dump itself, not just to internal statistics.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Before expiry, dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson() still lists the expected peer addresses; after the rolling window expires, those peers are removed and the JSON can collapse to {} when nothing current remains.

  '

FILE:rbf-dynamic-handler-allocation
title: 'HDFS-14750. RBF: Support dynamic handler allocation in routers'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Router-based Federation operators need fairness controls that can adapt handler capacity to real namespace traffic instead of staying fixed after startup. Static allocation can leave busy namespaces short on handlers while quieter namespaces hold unused capacity, which makes router throughput less responsive than it should be under uneven load.


  ## Desired outcome

  RBF should support a `DynamicRouterRpcFairnessPolicyController` that periodically resizes per-namespace permit capacity based on observed traffic while still enforcing configured minimum handler floors. The dynamic controller needs to honor the router handler-count settings, the minimum-per-namespace setting, and the refresh interval configuration, and it should expose the resulting capacity distribution through the existing permit-capacity JSON surface returned by `getPermitCapacityPerNs()` so operators and tests can observe the live allocation.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Routers can instantiate `DynamicRouterRpcFairnessPolicyController` as a fairness-policy option, per-namespace permit capacity is rebalanced over time according to traffic while preserving the configured minimum handler guarantees, the controller reports the current allocation through `getPermitCapacityPerNs()` as JSON, and permit acquisition behavior reflects the updated capacities rather than the static startup allocation.

  '

FILE:revert-rbf-handler-allocation
title: 'Revert "HDFS-14750. RBF: Support dynamic handler allocation in routers"'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS federation operators need router fairness controls to stay on the stable, predictable model rather than exposing a newer dynamic handler-allocation surface that is not ready to keep.

  ## Desired outcome

  The router should fall back to the pre-existing fairness behavior, without dynamic allocation classes, adjustable semaphores, or the extra per-namespace capacity and accept/reject metrics introduced by that experiment.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Existing permit acquisition and available-handler reporting continue to work, but the dynamic handler-allocation feature surface is absent.

  '

import subprocess, re
from pathlib import Path

            print(' ',d,h[:10],s)

FILE:peer-metrics-stale-records
title: HADOOP-17995. Stale record should be remove when DataNodePeerMetrics#dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  DataNode peer metrics are used for diagnosing downstream packet latency, but stale peers should not remain in the JSON dump after their rolling window has expired.


  ## Desired outcome

  `dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson` should drop stale records instead of continuing to report them.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The JSON output contains only peers with current rolling-average data rather than expired entries that confuse troubleshooting.

  '

FILE:remove-stale-peer-metrics
title: HADOOP-17995. Stale record should be remove when DataNodePeerMetrics#dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using DataNodePeerMetrics need dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson() to reflect only currently valid peer timing data. Stale entries should disappear once their rolling-average windows expire, otherwise the JSON keeps advertising dead peers as active.


  ## Desired outcome

  Restore stale-record removal for the peer downstream timing JSON while keeping active peers visible until their data truly expires. This should apply to the JSON dump itself, not just to internal statistics.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Before expiry, dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson() still lists the expected peer addresses; after the rolling window expires, those peers are removed and the JSON can collapse to {} when nothing current remains.

  '

FILE:revert-peer-metrics-pruning
title: Revert "HADOOP-17995. Stale record should be remove when DataNodePeerMetrics#dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson"
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  The recent change to aggressively prune stale entries from DataNode peer downstream timing JSON removed visibility that some operators and tests still depend on. This cleanup needs to be backed out until a safer semantics is defined.


  ## Desired outcome

  Revert the stale-record filtering change for DataNodePeerMetrics JSON output and restore the previous rolling-average behavior. This is an internal rollback intended to preserve existing observability contracts rather than introduce a new user-facing feature.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The peer timing JSON behaves the way it did before the reverted change, and the attempted stale-entry pruning no longer alters that exported view.

  '

FILE:active-tailer-jn-tolerance
title: HDFS-16689. NameNode may crash when transitioning to Active with in-progress tailer if there are some abnormal JNs.
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  During HA failover, a NameNode transitioning to active can still have an in-progress edit tailer, and abnormal JournalNodes in that window can trigger crashes instead of a controlled recovery path.


  ## Desired outcome

  Transitioning to active should tolerate abnormal JournalNode stream conditions during in-progress tailing without crashing the NameNode. Operators should see the transition either complete safely or fail in a controlled way, rather than losing the process because the tailer cannot handle the JournalNode state.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The edit-tailing path should be able to distinguish the durable-only case and avoid taking the NameNode down when JournalNode streams are abnormal during activation. HA transition behavior should remain stable for healthy JournalNodes.

  '

FILE:slow-datanode-metrics
title: HDFS-16526. Add metrics for slow DataNode
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators need clearer visibility into slow DataNode behavior so they can tell whether replication or write pipelines are being delayed by local disk work or by slow acknowledgements moving upstream through the pipeline. Without dedicated counters, these cases are harder to spot and diagnose from routine monitoring.


  ## Desired outcome

  DataNode metrics should expose separate counters for these slow-path conditions so monitoring systems can distinguish them directly. The exported metric contract needs to include `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` for delayed flush or sync activity and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount` for delayed upstream acknowledgements, without changing normal write behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  DataNode metrics now publish `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount`, slow flush-or-sync events increment the former, slow upstream-ack events increment the latter, and the change adds observability only without altering the underlying pipeline semantics.

  '

FILE:slow-datanode-metrics-docs
title: HDFS-16526. Addendum Add metrics for slow DataNode
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators can only make use of new DataNode slow-path counters if the metrics reference material describes them clearly enough to wire dashboards and alerts against the published names. After adding the slow DataNode metrics, the user-facing metrics documentation also needs to acknowledge those counters.


  ## Desired outcome

  Hadoop''s metrics reference should document the new slow DataNode counters so operators know that `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount` are available and what conditions they represent. This is documentation-only work, so runtime behavior and metric emission stay unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The metrics documentation includes the newly added slow DataNode counters by name, operators can discover `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount` from the published reference material, and no code behavior changes beyond that documentation update.

  '

FILE:setreplication-noop-editlog
title: HDFS-16531. Avoid setReplication writing an edit record if old replication equals the new value
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Some clients repeatedly call setReplication with the same replication value a file already has, which creates unnecessary NameNode work and extra edit-log traffic even though nothing is actually changing. At scale, these no-op requests add noise and overhead without improving file state.


  ## Desired outcome

  A set-replication request that does not change the current replication should still be treated as a successful operation from the caller''s perspective, but it should avoid writing an edit record or doing the heavier mutation path. Audit visibility should remain intact, and files should keep the same replication they already had.


  ## Acceptance signals

  No-op set-replication requests still succeed, the file''s replication remains unchanged, the NameNode avoids writing an unnecessary edit-log mutation for those no-op calls, and normal replication changes continue to follow the existing mutation path.

  '

FILE:router-getcontainers-federation
title: 'YARN-8900. [Router] Federation: routing getContainers REST invocations transparently to multiple RMs'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  In a federated YARN deployment, operators can already inspect application and attempt details through the Router, but container listings still stop at the individual ResourceManager boundary.


  ## Desired outcome

  When someone asks the Router for containers for an application attempt through `getContainers`, the Router should fan that request out to every active subcluster and return one merged `ContainersInfo` response instead of behaving as unimplemented. Invalid or unknown application or attempt identifiers should degrade cleanly to an empty container list rather than breaking the federated view.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A federated query for an application attempt spanning four active subclusters should come back with a single `ContainersInfo` whose `getContainers()` view contains all four containers. Requests for a nonexistent app, a malformed application id, or a malformed attempt id should return an empty `ContainersInfo`.

  '

FILE:external-sps-jmx-metrics
title: 'HDFS-16488. [SPS]: Expose metrics to JMX for external SPS'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators using the external Storage Policy Satisfier need standard JMX visibility into what that service is doing instead of relying only on logs.

  ## Desired outcome

  External SPS should publish a stable monitoring surface through `ExternalSPSMXBean`, backed by `ExternalSPSBeanMetrics`, so operators can inspect attempted movement state and related activity from ordinary JMX tooling.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The external SPS process initializes and closes its metrics cleanly, and the JMX surface exposes the attempted-item data needed for monitoring.

  '

FILE:revert-external-sps-jmx
title: 'Revert "HDFS-16488. [SPS]: Expose metrics to JMX for external SPS"'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators running the external Storage Policy Satisfier need the service itself to keep working, but they do not want a newly added JMX surface that is not ready to remain part of the supported management contract.

  ## Desired outcome

  External SPS should continue operating without exposing `ExternalSPSBeanMetrics` or the `ExternalSPSMXBean` management interface, and the attempted-item internals that were temporarily made public should go back to being internal implementation detail.

  ## Acceptance signals

  There is no JMX bean published for external SPS, while the command-line and runtime behavior of the service stay aligned with the pre-metrics implementation.

  '

FILE:s3a-public-dataset-testutils
title: HADOOP-18168. Fix S3A ITestMarkerTool dep. on purged public bucket, introduce PublicDatasetTestUtils
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The S3A public-dataset tests currently depend on a bucket layout that has been cleaned up, which makes previously stable requester-pays and marker-tool coverage unreliable. Test maintainers need those suites to point at a still-valid public dataset and to have one place that defines which public bucket and object should be used for each scenario.


  ## Desired outcome

  The S3A test utilities should provide a shared `PublicDatasetTestUtils` helper that supplies the configured public-dataset locations for cases such as requester-pays access and large public buckets with many objects. The default requester-pays path should move to a working public dataset, while still allowing environments to override those locations or skip the tests where requester-pays or AWS-specific assumptions do not apply.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The requester-pays coverage uses a valid public object again, marker-tool tests can obtain their public dataset locations through `PublicDatasetTestUtils`, configurable overrides remain available for different environments, and incompatible environments can skip these dataset-dependent tests instead of failing against a purged bucket.

  '

}

    for line in out.splitlines():
        h,ct,ad,s=line.split('\\t',3)
        if h not in commit_by_hash:
            commit_by_hash[h]={'hash':h,'timestamp':int(ct),'date':ad,'subject':s,'branches':[br]}
        else:
            commit_by_hash[h]['branches'].append(br)
all_commits=list(commit_by_hash.values())

    return min(branch_pref.get(br,99) for br in commit['branches'])

def normalize(text):

    if (text.startswith(\"'\") and text.endswith(\"'\")) or (text.startswith('\"') and text.endswith('\"')):
        text=text[1:-1]
    text=text.replace(\"''\", \"'\")
    text=text.replace('…','...')
    text=text.replace('’',\"'\").replace('“','\"').replace('”','\"')
    text=re.sub(r'\\s*\\(#\\d+\\)"'$'"','',text)
    text=re.sub(r'"'^'"\\[["'^'"\\]]+\\]\\s*','',text)
    text=re.sub(r'\\s+',' ',text)
    return text.strip()

def strip_jira(text):
    t=normalize(text)
    t=re.sub(r'"'^[A-Za-z]+-'"\\d+[:.]?\\s*','',t)
    return t.strip()

reqs=[]
for f in sorted(Path('/workspace/requirements').glob('*.yaml')):
    txt=f.read_text()
    raw=re.search(r'"'^title:'"\\s*(.*)"'$'"', txt, re.M).group(1).strip()
    reqs.append({'slug':f.stem,'raw_title':raw,'title':normalize(raw)})

mapping=[]
unresolved=[]
for r in reqs:
    if r['slug'] in manual:
        hashes=manual[r['slug']]
        mapping.append({'slug':r['slug'],'hashes':hashes,'title':r['title'],'manual':True})
        continue
    title=r['title']
    stripped=strip_jira(title)
    jira_m=re.search(r'([A-Za-z]+-\\d+)', title)
    jira=jira_m.group(1) if jira_m else None

    candidates=[]
    # exact title match first
    for c in all_commits:
        subj=normalize(c['subject'])
        if subj == title:
            candidates.append((0.0,c))
    if not candidates:
        for c in all_commits:
            subj=normalize(c['subject'])
            if strip_jira(subj) == stripped:
                candidates.append((0.0,c))
    if not candidates and jira:
        jira_pool=[c for c in all_commits if jira.lower() in c['subject'].lower()]
        for c in jira_pool:
            ratio=SequenceMatcher(None, stripped.lower(), strip_jira(c['subject']).lower()).ratio()
            if ratio >= 0.52:
                candidates.append((1-ratio,c))
    if not candidates:
        # fuzzy over all commits for no-jira-subject oddities
        for c in all_commits:
            ratio=SequenceMatcher(None, stripped.lower(), strip_jira(c['subject']).lower()).ratio()
            if ratio >= 0.88:
                candidates.append((1-ratio,c))
    if not candidates:
        unresolved.append(r)
        continue
    # rank by exact/fuzzy score, branch preference, and subject closeness
    uniq={}
    for score,c in candidates:
        prev=uniq.get(c['hash'])
        if prev is None or score<prev:
            uniq[c['hash']]=score
    ranked=[]
    for h,score in uniq.items():
        c=commit_by_hash[h]
        ranked.append((score,best_branch(c),abs(c['timestamp']),c))
    ranked.sort(key=lambda x:(x[0],x[1],x[2]))
    chosen=ranked[0][3]
    mapping.append({'slug':r['slug'],'hashes':[chosen['hash']],'title':r['title'],'manual':False,'subject':chosen['subject'],'branches':chosen['branches']})

print('mapped', len(mapping), 'unresolved', len(unresolved))
for r in unresolved:
    print('UNRESOLVED', r['slug'], r['title'])
# check duplicate slug count and hash coverage stats
print('manual', sum(1 for m in mapping if m.get('manual')))
# write mapping
Path('/tmp/requirement_commit_map.json').write_text(json.dumps(mapping, indent=2))
print('wrote /tmp/requirement_commit_map.json')

            ratio=SequenceMatcher(None, stripped.lower(), strip_jira(c['subject']).lower()).ratio()
            if ratio >= 0.88:
                candidates.append((1-ratio,c))
    if not candidates:
        unresolved.append(r)
        continue
    # rank by exact/fuzzy score, branch preference, and subject closeness
    uniq={}
    for score,c in candidates:
        prev=uniq.get(c['hash'])
        if prev is None or score<prev:
            uniq[c['hash']]=score
    ranked=[]
    for h,score in uniq.items():
        c=commit_by_hash[h]
        ranked.append((score,best_branch(c),abs(c['timestamp']),c))
    ranked.sort(key=lambda x:(x[0],x[1],x[2]))
    chosen=ranked[0][3]
    mapping.append({'slug':r['slug'],'hashes':[chosen['hash']],'title':r['title'],'manual':False,'subject':chosen['subject'],'branches':chosen['branches']})

print('mapped', len(mapping), 'unresolved', len(unresolved))
for r in unresolved:
    print('UNRESOLVED', r['slug'], r['title'])
# check duplicate slug count and hash coverage stats
print('manual', sum(1 for m in mapping if m.get('manual')))
# write mapping
Path('/tmp/requirement_commit_map.json').write_text(json.dumps(mapping, indent=2))
print('wrote /tmp/requirement_commit_map.json')
PY"

import json, os

    break
  fi
done < /tmp/remaining_slug_hashes.txt

echo "COMPLETED $count"
'"'"

item.aggregated_output:
Router supports assignment of the dedicated number of RPC handlers to achieve isolation for all downstream nameservices it is configured to proxy. Since large or busy clusters may have relatively higher RPC traffic to the namenode compared to other clusters namenodes, this feature if enabled allows admins to configure higher number of RPC handlers for busy clusters. If dedicated handlers are not assigned for specific nameservices, equal distribution of RPC handlers is done for all configured nameservices. **Note** Fanout calls are treated as targeting a special nameservice, thus can be configured with handlers as well.

If a downstream namenode is slow/busy enough that permits are unavailable, routers would throw StandByException exception to the client. This would in turn trigger a failover behavior at the client side and clients would connect to a different router in the cluster. This offers a positive effect of automatically load balancing RPCs across all routers nodes. This is important to ensure that a single router does not become a bottleneck in case of unhealthy namenodes and all handlers available in the entire router cluster are utilized.

Users can configure handlers based on steady state load that individual downstream namenodes expect and can introduce more routers to the cluster to handle more RPCs overall. Because of the bouncing behavior that clients automatically get in this feature in an event where certain namenodes are overloaded, good clients connecting to good namenodes will always continue to use Rpc lanes dedicated to them. For bad behaving namenodes or backfill jobs that put spiky loads on namenodes, more routers could potentially be added with a higher than usual handler count to deal with the surge in traffic for specific nameservices if needed.

Overall the isolation feature is exposed via a configuration dfs.federation.router.handler.isolation.enable. The default value of this feature will be “false”. Users can also introduce their own fairness policy controller for custom allocation of handlers to various nameservices.

See the Apache JIRA ticket [HDFS-14090](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HDFS-14090) for more information on this feature.

HDFS Router-based Federation
============================

<!-- MACRO{toc|fromDepth=0|toDepth=3} -->

Introduction
------------

NameNodes have scalability limits because of the metadata overhead comprised of inodes (files and directories) and file blocks, the number of Datanode heartbeats, and the number of HDFS RPC client requests.
The common solution is to split the filesystem into smaller subclusters [HDFS Federation](../hadoop-hdfs/Federation.html) and provide a federated view [ViewFs](../hadoop-hdfs/ViewFs.html).
The problem is how to maintain the split of the subclusters (e.g., namespace partition), which forces users to connect to multiple subclusters and manage the allocation of folders/files to them.


Architecture
------------

A natural extension to this partitioned federation is to add a layer of software responsible for federating the namespaces.
This extra layer allows users to access any subcluster transparently, lets subclusters manage their own block pools independently, and will support rebalancing of data across subclusters later
(see more info in [HDFS-13123](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HDFS-13123)). The subclusters in RBF are not required to be the independent HDFS clusters, a normal federation cluster
(with multiple block pools) or a mixed cluster with federation and independent cluster is also allowed.
To accomplish these goals, the federation layer directs block accesses to the proper subcluster, maintains the state of the namespaces, and provides mechanisms for data rebalancing.
This layer must be scalable, highly available, and fault tolerant.

This federation layer comprises multiple components.
The _Router_ component that has the same interface as a NameNode, and forwards the client requests to the correct subcluster, based on ground-truth information from a State Store.
The _State Store_ combines a remote _Mount Table_ (in the flavor of [ViewFs](../hadoop-hdfs/ViewFs.html), but shared between clients) and utilization (load/capacity) information about the subclusters.
This approach has the same architecture as [YARN federation](../../hadoop-yarn/hadoop-yarn-site/Federation.html).

![Router-based Federation Sequence Diagram | width=800](./images/routerfederation.png)


### Example flow
The simplest configuration deploys a Router on each NameNode machine.
The Router monitors the local NameNode and its state and heartbeats to the State Store.
The Router monitors the local NameNode and heartbeats the state to the State Store.
When a regular DFS client contacts any of the Routers to access a file in the federated filesystem, the Router checks the Mount Table in the State Store (i.e., the local cache) to find out which subcluster contains the file.
Then it checks the Membership table in the State Store (i.e., the local cache) for the NameNode responsible for the subcluster.
After it has identified the correct NameNode, the Router proxies the request.
The client accesses Datanodes directly.


### Router
There can be multiple Routers in the system with soft state.
Each Router has two roles:

* Federated interface: expose a single, global NameNode interface to the clients and forward the requests to the active NameNode in the correct subcluster
* NameNode heartbeat: maintain the information about a NameNode in the State Store

#### Federated interface
The Router receives a client request, checks the State Store for the correct subcluster, and forwards the request to the active NameNode of that subcluster.
The reply from the NameNode then flows in the opposite direction.
The Routers are stateless and can be behind a load balancer. For health checking, you can use /isActive endpoint as a health probe (e.g. http://ROUTER_HOSTNAME:ROUTER_PORT/isActive).
For performance, the Router also caches remote mount table entries and the state of the subclusters.
To make sure that changes have been propagated to all Routers, each Router heartbeats its state to the State Store.

The communications between the Routers and the State Store are cached (with timed expiration for freshness).
This improves the performance of the system.

#### Router heartbeat
The Router periodically heartbeats its state to the State Store.

#### NameNode heartbeat
For this role, the Router periodically checks the state of a NameNode (usually on the same server) and reports their high availability (HA) state and load/space status to the State Store.
Note that this is an optional role, as a Router can be independent of any subcluster.
For performance with NameNode HA, the Router uses the high availability state information in the State Store to forward the request to the NameNode that is most likely to be active.
Note that this service can be embedded into the NameNode itself to simplify the operation.

#### Availability and fault tolerance
The Router operates with failures at multiple levels.

* **Federated interface HA:**
The Routers are stateless and metadata operations are atomic at the NameNodes.
If a Router becomes unavailable, any Router can take over for it.
The clients configure their DFS HA client (e.g., ConfiguredFailoverProvider or RequestHedgingProxyProvider) with all the Routers in the federation as endpoints.

* **Unavailable State Store:**
If a Router cannot contact the State Store, it will enter into a Safe Mode state which disallows it from serving requests.
Clients will treat Routers in Safe Mode as it was an Standby NameNode and try another Router. There is a manual way to manage the Safe Mode for the Router.

The Safe Mode state can be managed by using the following command:

    [hdfs]$ $HADOOP_HOME/bin/hdfs dfsrouteradmin -safemode enter | leave | get

* **NameNode heartbeat HA:**
For high availability and flexibility, multiple Routers can monitor the same NameNode and heartbeat the information to the State Store.
This increases clients' resiliency to stale information, should a Router fail.
Conflicting NameNode information in the State Store is resolved by each Router via a quorum.

* **Unavailable NameNodes:**
If a Router cannot contact the active NameNode, then it will try the other NameNodes in the subcluster.
It will first try those reported as standby and then the unavailable ones.
If the Router cannot reach any NameNode, then it throws an exception.

* **Expired NameNodes:**
If a NameNode heartbeat has not been recorded in the State Store for a multiple of the heartbeat interval, the monitoring Router will record that the NameNode has expired and no Routers will attempt to access it.
If an updated heartbeat is subsequently recorded for the NameNode, the monitoring Router will restore the NameNode from the expired state.

#### Interfaces
To interact with the users and the administrators, the Router exposes multiple interfaces.

* **RPC:**
The Router RPC implements the most common interfaces clients use to interact with HDFS.
The current implementation has been tested using analytics workloads written in plain MapReduce, Spark, and Hive (on Tez, Spark, and MapReduce).
Advanced functions like snapshot, encryption and tiered storage are left for future versions.
All unimplemented functions will throw exceptions.

The prompt which is then presented is located at a mounted version of the source tree

Note that from within this docker environment you ONLY have access to the Hadoop source

  An alternative solution to this problem is to install Linux native inside a virtual machine

Refer to  dev-support/docker/Dockerfile):

* Open JDK 1.8
  $ sudo apt-get update
  $ sudo apt-get -y install java-8-openjdk
* Maven
  $ sudo apt-get -y install maven
* Native libraries
  $ sudo apt-get -y install build-essential autoconf automake libtool cmake zlib1g-dev pkg-config libssl-dev libsasl2-dev
* GCC 9.3.0
  $ sudo apt-get -y install software-properties-common
  $ sudo add-apt-repository -y ppa:ubuntu-toolchain-r/test
  $ sudo apt-get update
  $ sudo apt-get -y install g++-9 gcc-9
  $ sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/gcc gcc /usr/bin/gcc-9 60 --slave /usr/bin/g++ g++ /usr/bin/g++-9
* CMake 3.19
  $ curl -L https://cmake.org/files/v3.19/cmake-3.19.0.tar.gz > cmake-3.19.0.tar.gz
  $ tar -zxvf cmake-3.19.0.tar.gz && cd cmake-3.19.0
  $ ./bootstrap
  $ make -j$(nproc)
  $ sudo make install
* Protocol Buffers 3.7.1 (required to build native code)
  $ curl -L -s -S https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/download/v3.7.1/protobuf-java-3.7.1.tar.gz -o protobuf-3.7.1.tar.gz
  $ mkdir protobuf-3.7-src
  $ tar xzf protobuf-3.7.1.tar.gz --strip-components 1 -C protobuf-3.7-src && cd protobuf-3.7-src
  $ ./configure
  $ make -j$(nproc)
  $ sudo make install
* Boost
  $ curl -L https://sourceforge.net/projects/boost/files/boost/1.72.0/boost_1_72_0.tar.bz2/download > boost_1_72_0.tar.bz2
  $ tar --bzip2 -xf boost_1_72_0.tar.bz2 && cd boost_1_72_0
  $ ./bootstrap.sh --prefix=/usr/
  $ ./b2 --without-python
  $ sudo ./b2 --without-python install

* Snappy compression (only used for hadoop-mapreduce-client-nativetask)

* Linux FUSE

* ZStandard compression

Date:   Fri Mar 11 13:05:45 2022 +0530

    HADOOP-18112: Implement paging during multi object delete. (#4045)
    
    
    Multi object delete of size more than 1000 is not supported by S3 and
    fails with MalformedXML error. So implementing paging of requests to
    reduce the number of keys in a single request. Page size can be configured
    using "fs.s3a.bulk.delete.page.size"
    
     Contributed By: Mukund Thakur
